You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Project: tparse

Description:
A command-line tool that analyzes and summarizes test-run output in JSON format and presents
readable, grouped summaries of failures, panics, and package-level statistics. It helps
quickly surface failing tests and provides an optional table of passed/skipped tests with
elapsed times.

Usage:
- Provide test output in JSON format (from your test runner) to the program via stdin or a
  file. The tool reads the JSON event stream and prints a concise summary of failures and
  an optional table of test results.

Examples:
- Pipe a JSON test output stream into the program and display a full summary.
  <your-test-runner> --json | tparse -all

- Save JSON output to a file and run:
  tparse -all -file=tests.json

Options (selected user-facing):
- -all: display passed and skipped tests in addition to failures
- -pass: display passed tests
- -skip: display skipped tests
- -file: read JSON test output from a file
- -follow: stream raw test output alongside processed summary
- -nocolor: disable colored output
- -smallscreen: format long test names for narrow terminals

For full usage, run: tparse -h

import subprocess, json, sys
def ev(action, package=None, test=None, output=None, elapsed=None, time=None):
    d={}
    if time is not None: d["Time"]=time
    d["Action"]=action
    if package is not None: d["Package"]=package
    if test is not None: d["Test"]=test
    if output is not None: d["Output"]=output
    if elapsed is not None: d["Elapsed"]=elapsed
    return d
def write(events, path="/tmp/synth.json"):
    with open(path,"w") as f:
        for e in events:
            f.write(json.dumps(e)+"\n")
    return path
def run(args, path="/tmp/synth.json"):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args+["-file="+path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("exit", r.returncode)
    print("STDOUT:")
    print(r.stdout, end="")
    if r.stderr:
        print("STDERR:")
        print(r.stderr, end="")
    return r

import subprocess, json
def ev(action, package=None, test=None, output=None, elapsed=None, time=None):

    d["Action"]=action
    if package is not None: d["Package"]=package

    with open(path,"wb") as f:

                f.write(e.encode() if isinstance(e,str) else e)
            else:
                f.write(json.dumps(e).encode()+b"\n")
    return path
def lines_of(b):
    parts=[]; start=0
    while True:
        i=b.find(b'\n',start)
        if i==-1:
            if start<len(b): parts.append(b[start:])
            break
        parts.append(b[start:i+1]); start=i+1
    return parts
def run(args, path="/tmp/synth.json", stdin_data=None):
    cmd=["/workspace/executable"]+args
    if path is not None: cmd+=["-file="+path]
    r=subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, input=stdin_data)
    print("exit",r.returncode)
    print("STDOUT:")
    for p in lines_of(r.stdout): print(repr(p.decode('utf-8', 'backslashreplace')))
    if r.stderr: print("STDERR:", repr(r.stderr.decode('utf-8','backslashreplace')))

def pkg(name,kind):
    if kind=="R": return [ev("pass",name,"TestX",elapsed=0.01), ev("pass",name,None,elapsed=0.1)]
    if kind=="Rnotestcount": # regular no tests, pass

    if kind=="Nfiles": return [ev("output",name,None,f"?   \t{name}\t[no test files]\n"), ev("skip",name,None,elapsed=0)]
    if kind=="Nrun": return [ev("output",name,None,f"ok  \t{name}\t0.1s [no tests to run]\n"), ev("pass",name,None,elapsed=0.1)]
    if kind=="Z": return [ev("output",name,None,"coverage: 0.0% of statements\n"), ev("pass",name,None,elapsed=0.1)]
    if kind=="E": return [ev("start",name)]
    if kind=="Panic": return [ev("output",name,"TestP","panic: x\n"), ev("fail",name,None,elapsed=0.1)]
    raise ValueError(kind)
def summary(combo, args=["-nocolor"]):

import subprocess, os, json
def runfile(data, args=["-nocolor"]):
    open("/tmp/in.json","wb").write(data if isinstance(data,bytes) else data.encode())
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args+["-file=/tmp/in.json"], capture_output=True)
    print("input",repr(data[:200]),"=> exit",r.returncode,"out",r.stdout[:500],"err",r.stderr)
def runstdin(data,args=["-nocolor"]):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args, input=data if isinstance(data,bytes) else data.encode(), capture_output=True)

good='{"Action":"pass","Package":"pkg/a","Elapsed":0.1}\n'
runfile(good)
runfile(good.rstrip("\n"))
runfile("\n\n"+good+"\n\n")
runfile("not json\n"+good)
runfile('{"Action":"pass",}\n'+good)
runfile('{"Action":123,"Package":"pkg/a"}\n'+good)
runfile('{"action":"pass","package":"pkg/a","elapsed":0.1}\n')
runfile('{"ACTION":"pass","PACKAGE":"pkg/a","ELAPSED":0.1}\n')
runfile('{"Action":"PASS","Package":"pkg/a","Elapsed":0.1}\n')
runfile('{"Action":"pass","Package":"pkg/a","Test":"TestX","Elapsed":"0.1"}\n')
runfile('{"Action":"pass","Package":"pkg/a","Elapsed":0.1,"Extra":123}\n')
runfile('[]\n')
runfile('123\n')
runfile('"string"\n')
runfile('null\n')
runfile('{}\n')
runfile('{"Time":"bad"}\n'+good)
runfile('{"Time":123}\n'+good)
runfile(good+"trailing garbage without newline")
runfile(good+'{"Action":"fail","Package":"pkg/b","Elapsed":0.2}') # no newline between? actually good ends \n, second no \n EOF
runfile(good.strip()+'{"Action":"fail","Package":"pkg/b"}') # two JSON on one line no newline separation
runfile('  '+good)
runfile('\t'+good)
runfile(good.replace("\n","\r\n"))
runfile(b'\xff\xfe'+good.encode())
runfile(b'\xef\xbb\xbf'+good.encode())
runfile('{"Action":"pass","Package":"pkg/a","Elapsed":1e999}\n') # overflow float?
runfile('{"Action":"pass","Package":"pkg/a","Elapsed":NaN}\n')
# very long line
longout='{"Action":"output","Package":"pkg/a","Test":"TestX","Output":"'+"x"*200000+'\\n"}\n'+good
runfile(longout)
longout2='{"Action":"output","Package":"pkg/a","Test":"TestX","Output":"'+"x"*70000+'\\n"}\n'+good
runfile(longout2)
PY

"}
